Subject: Hybrid boardroom accreditation + concurrent translation — quick feasibility

Hi team,

We are finalizing room selection for an Acme Corp executive workshop on Jul 22–23 and need a quick feasibility check from venue + AV vendor on two items before we lock space:

1) Boardroom accreditation: the client requires a 20-person boardroom that supports simultaneous desktop view for remote execs (Zoom + SIP gateway) with prioritized low-latency audio. We need confirmation of mic count, Dante/analog splits, and redundancy options.

2) Concurrent translation: Acme will have Mandarin->English and English->Mandarin live translation streams for four breakout rooms and the main boardroom. We need to confirm interpreters' booth, channel routing, and latency SLA for remote participants (max 250ms). Can you outline equipment/codec requirements and whether any RF frequency coordination is required?

Ballpark budget for AV + interpretation is TBD; at this stage we just need a technical fit and anything that would disqualify the boardroom (e.g., no separate interpreter booth, ISP constraints).

Please reply with a short feasibility note and any blockers by EOD today so we can update Acme and select alternates if needed.

Thanks,

--
Mina Haddad

Subject: Re: Hybrid boardroom accreditation + concurrent translation — quick feasibility

Hi Mina / all,

Short answer: feasible. High-level notes below — happy to jump on a 20-min call to walk through wiring diagrams.

• Boardroom: the room in RP floor 7 supports 20 seats, has dual Dante zones, an AV mixer capable of two independent program busses, and a redundant audio DSP. We recommend 8 boundary mics + 4 shotgun spot mics for panelists to preserve spatial pickup.

• Conferencing: we can do Zoom + SIP trunking. For low-latency, we'll use an on-site MCU with a direct peering to our cloud bridge (we've achieved 180–220ms in similar setups).

• Translation: we provide a portable interpreter booth for the main boardroom and two rolling booths for breakouts. We output 3 isolated channels (main, ch1 Mandarin, ch2 English) via AES67/Dante and can route to Zoom audio channels. Latency to remote is ~200–250ms end-to-end depending on the client's network.

Blockers / ask:
• ISP: need confirmed outbound bandwidth of 40 Mbps sustained on the event VLAN.
• RF: we'll use wireless mics on 5 GHz; venue must confirm not to run heavy 5G small cells in the hall.
• Power: two N+1 UPS circuits in the AV rack required.

Attaching a brief spec sheet for translation consoles.

Best,
Alex — Ops Lead, Nimble AV
ops@nimbleav.com

Quick technical addendum for the rehearsal and day-of: 

• Codec choices: prefer OPUS for Zoom channels and PCM for interpreter routing internal to the AV stack. If Nimble's onboard booth uses AES67 we will need a bridging node.
• SIP fallback: supply of a secondary SIP trunk (different provider) recommended to reduce single-provider failure risk.
• QoS: event VLAN must mark RTP DSCP EF (0x2E) and ensure end-to-end queuing.
• Test accounts: one Zoom Pro staging account, SIP test trunk credentials (username/pass), and a temporary interpreter user for the bridge.

If Nimble can provide a channel map + sample pcap from a prior event, that would drastically speed up our rehearsal validation.

—Karthik
